title: Paper Towels 6-roll

drivers.name: Promotion: 20% off
drivers.evidence: Noise-adjusted uplift from 18 past promotions: x2.09; deeper discount (16.4% vs 20%) and past x3.32 in similar context, but competition reduces lift.

drivers.name: Competitor store opening across the street
drivers.evidence: Planner note indicates new competitor; historical data shows 10-30% sales erosion from similar events; no prior data for this product, but plausible based on category.

adjustment.analysis: The 20% off promotion has a strong historical uplift of x2.09 (noise-adjusted) from 18 past occurrences, but the current price drop is deeper (16.4% vs 20% off), and the product sold x3.32 during a 30% off + back-to-school week. However, a competitor opening across the street introduces demand cannibalization risk. The baseline already reflects seasonal trends and recent price spikes. The uplift is likely capped by competition. Shrink the model's x2.09 to x1.75 to account for noise, competition, and a partial price effect. Downside spread widens slightly due to uncertainty.

brief:
PRODUCT: Paper Towels 6-roll | category Household | Store #12 (Austin, TX)
TARGET WEEK: 2026-10-12 to 2026-10-18 (next week)

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:
  events: Promotion: 20% off
  shelf price: 8.26 (-16.4% vs regular price 9.88)
  planner notes: A competitor opens a store across the street this week

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 96.6 | 5%-95%: 62.9 - 233.3 | 10%-90%: 67.4 - 191.2

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-23% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
